item: `holdover-rate-tn` (rule 53 as amended 2026-09-30): check when its figure applies, not only its size. (a) Virginia's holdover rate was lawful in amount but started 'after this Lease otherwise ends' where the statute starts it at the landlord's notice date: confirm this state's trigger is one its law allows. (b) Alabama found the clause starts the charge only 'after the end of the Term', so a landlord loses it after an earlier termination (for breach, or a month-to-month notice); where this state's law allows it, extend the trigger to any termination, and record the verdict. (c) If you extend the trigger to an earlier termination, apply rule 53's two later sentences too: exclude a termination for nonpayment of Rent where the late fee is capped or the tenant can keep possession by paying after the termination (as amended 1.38, from GA's circle-back; `holdover-rate-ga` and `holdover-rate-nc` are the wording), and if a court can double or treble holdover damages, say the charge isn't recovered for any day a statutory multiple is (as amended 1.43, from MO's circle-back; `holdover-rate-mo`). Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-512(c) in the 17 Act counties; other counties separately.

Tenant-chore split (SOP rule 48 as amended 1.21, found at ND's retro 2026-10-02): does your landlord-tenant act let the lease shift maintenance tasks (mowing, snow removal) to the tenant only for a single-family residence, and require a separate signed writing with its own consideration for any other dwelling (the uniform act's split; Arizona, Nebraska, Iowa and North Dakota have it)? If so, add a note to your segments of `landscaping-irrigation` and `snow-removal` that they bind only for a single-family residence, and, since Tennessee already has `tenant-repair-agreement-tn`, rebuild that row on the `maintenance-allocation-az` / `maintenance-allocation-nd` pattern (named tasks, a consideration blank, the separate-document instruction, the statute's no-condition rule) rather than adding a second clause on the same topic (SOP rule 48 as amended 1.33, AL's lesson). This is settled (rule 48); don't ask Taylor. If your act has no such split, record that in one line.

Holdover rate (SOP rule 54; decided by Claude Code at the 2026-10-02 SD sync, rule 76, on your own recommendation): add an optional CONDITIONAL `holdover-rate-sd`, never a default, modelled on `holdover-rate-ga`. SDCL §§ 43-32-14 and 43-32-15 give no damages measure for holding over, so the lease can set one; SDCL §§ 53-9-4 and 53-9-5 mean it must approximate actual loss (daily Rent plus documented re-letting loss), not a multiple. Decide whether its trigger reaches an earlier termination, and exclude a termination for nonpayment if a daily charge would work as a second late charge (rule 53 as amended 1.23).

Rule 62 vetting, shared rows (queued at the CA retro sync, 2026-10-03; answer each, shared text not edited): (1) `surrender-end-of-term` (CA's proposal, 2026-10-03): qualify 'Tenant will surrender possession of the property and return all keys to Landlord immediately' with 'unless applicable law entitles Tenant to remain', because a just-cause or similar statute may let a tenant stay past the term. Is the qualified wording lawful and accurate in your state, and does the current wording state a duty your law doesn't back? (2) `default-by-tenant` (MN's proposal, 2026-10-02; ND and CA support): move the no-cure carve-out ('except where applicable law permits Landlord to proceed without giving Tenant an opportunity to cure') out of the non-rent limb into its own sentence reaching both limbs. Is that lawful and accurate in your state (it is self-limiting, so check only that it can't be read to drop a cure or pre-suit notice your law requires for nonpayment)? Already settled, so don't ask Taylor again: if the edit would only drop the lease's own promise of written notice of a rent default that your law doesn't require, Taylor decided for Indiana (2026-10-03) and Pennsylvania (2026-10-04) that the lease follows the statute, with no optional notice clause. Support the edit, and say in your section which education row should tell landlords they may still give notice first (Claude Code updates it at the merge).
